didascalie.title: The Etruscan kings
didascalie.line: They drain the marshes between the hills. The Forum is born.

didascalie.title: No more kings
didascalie.line: The last king is driven out. Rome becomes a republic.

didascalie.title: The Gauls sack Rome
didascalie.line: Only the Capitoline Hill holds out.

didascalie.title: The Appian Way
didascalie.line: The first great Roman road, and the first aqueduct.

didascalie.title: Carthage destroyed
didascalie.line: Rome now rules the Mediterranean.

didascalie.title: The Ides of March
didascalie.line: Julius Caesar is murdered in the Senate.

didascalie.title: Augustus, first emperor
didascalie.line: "I found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble."

didascalie.title: The Great Fire
didascalie.line: Ten of the fourteen districts burn. Nero rebuilds.

didascalie.title: The empire at its largest
didascalie.line: From Scotland to Iraq, ruled from this city.

didascalie.title: A million people
didascalie.line: The largest city the world has ever seen.

didascalie.title: A new capital
didascalie.line: Constantine moves the emperor to Constantinople.

didascalie.title: The end of the Western Empire
didascalie.line: The last emperor in the West is deposed.

didascalie.title: Plague and floods
didascalie.line: Fewer than 50,000 people live inside walls built for a million.

didascalie.title: Charlemagne
didascalie.line: Crowned emperor in Old St Peter's on Christmas Day.

didascalie.title: The Normans
didascalie.line: Allies of the Pope burn much of the city.

didascalie.title: The Popes leave
didascalie.line: The papacy moves to Avignon. Rome falls to ~17,000 people.

didascalie.title: The Popes return
didascalie.line: Rome starts to grow again, around the Vatican.

didascalie.title: The Sack of Rome
didascalie.line: Charles V's unpaid troops loot the city for months.

didascalie.title: Trevi Fountain
didascalie.line: Finished after 30 years of work.

didascalie.title: Napoleon
didascalie.line: French troops arrive. The Pope is taken prisoner.

didascalie.title: March on Rome
didascalie.line: Mussolini takes power.

didascalie.title: Liberation
didascalie.line: Allied troops enter Rome on 4 June 1944.
